newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Slow economy, new plant hits Australia's Fairfax.
newsitem.headline: Slow economy, new plant hits Australia's Fairfax.

text.p: Australia's oldest newspaper publisher John Fairfax Holdings Ltd reported a 17-percent fall in annual profits on Wednesday, blaming a slow economy and higher costs from a new printing plant for the slide.

Fairfax, about 22 percent owned by New Zealand's Brierley Investments Ltd, said pre-abnormals net profit was A$85 million (US$63 million) in the year to June 30, 1997, down from A$102.2 million a year ago.
"This reflects approximately A$50 million of higher depreciation and interest expenses primarily arising from the completion of the Chullora printing facility," Fairfax said in its results statement.
The Chullora plant in Western Sydney was built for A$330 million over 1995 and 1996 to allow Fairfax to print more colour photographs in its newspapers.
Net profit after abnormals fell 15.4 percent to A$74 million after abnormal losses of A$11 million for redundancy and restructure costs.
Overall advertising volumes at Fairfax's The Sydney Morning Herald, The Australian Financial Review and The Age daily newspapers fell two percent.
"Classified advertising volumes were down by about two percent, mainly due to the lower real estate volumes offset by improvements in employment and motor," Fairfax said.
Analysts had forecast Fairfax would report a net profit before abnormals of around A$90.3 million.
Fairfax's shares closed down one cent at A$3.18 on the result, which was slightly below market expectations.
